title: [Bug]: Search failed when we insert data into Milvus, both datanode and querynode keep crashing
body: ### Is there an existing issue for this? - [X] I have searched the existing issues ### Environment ```markdown - Milvus version: 2.3.3 - Deployment mode(standalone or cluster): cluster - MQ type(rocksmq, pulsar or kafka): kafka - SDK version(e.g. pymilvus v2.0.0rc2): pymilvus 2.3.2 - OS(Ubuntu or CentOS): AWS Linux - CPU/Memory:12 * 8C64G for query node, 1 * 4C8G for data node. - GPU: No GPU - Others: ``` ### Current Behavior We started a 2.2.3 cluster with 12 * 8C64GB query nodes to store a big vector set, but we found the cluster is not stable. - The search will fail when writing data into Milvus, the failed message is like `failed to search: leader not available: lastHB=2023-11-21 01:55:07.499389221 +0000 UTC: node=989: node offline: channel=by-dev-rootcoord-dml_9_445714102417550498v0: channel not available`. - Most of the query nodes keep failing, the data node also crashes frequently, the memory usage of the nodes changed very quickly, see pictures below. ### Expected Behavior We expect the search can work normally when we're inserting data. ### Steps To Reproduce _No response_ ### Milvus Log [milvus-log.tar.gz](https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus/files/13421047/milvus-log.tar.gz) ### Anything else? _No response_

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant2 Thanks for the reply.

1. We use Flink job to `upsert` the data because we'd like to keep the identity for the same id, the parallelism is set `5`, batch size is 10000.
2. We have 14 fields, the primary key is `varchar` type, the embedding field is 1536 dim with IVF_FLAT index type (`nlist= 16384`) , the other 12 fields are varchar/int/float as potential filter conditions. I also noticed the scalar fields have Trie or STL_SORT index, not sure if it's related.
3. The resource for data node is 4C8G and 2C13G for Kafka. (Both requests and limits)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
@participant3 Do you think adding resource will help?

FYI:

- We notice this error at the early stage of the ingestion. At that time the memory usage of query nodes is less than 10G.
- The memory usage of data node seems keep increasing recently (and may be killed due to OOM later). Not sure this is as expected or memory leak happens.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I think the insert throughput is too heavy, that causes 1) datanode is not able to flush the data in time; 2) indexnode is not able to build index for all the segments, and the querynodes have to load growing segments(without index); which causes OOM.
My suggestion is
1. reduce the insert throughput to 20MB/s
2. add 3 more indexnode(the more cpu cores, the faster in building index)
3. if you changed the shard_number in collection schema, add more datanodes to make it equals to the shard_number

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
> @participant2 @reporter `socket.connection.setup.timeout.ms` added in this PR https://github.com/milvus-io/milvus/pull/26686/files#diff-708136128f96993332a36f4ae9725c1bd66b50c092c7f5fe39b61be225e5ee24

The issue is that we set a value of a config key to int64, here is timeout, however, the kafka client requires the type to be bool, int, or string. We can disable the config now and change the value type to string or int later.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
It appears the primary issue with Milvus stems from high insert throughput causing data node crashes and query node instability. The recent fix related to `socket.connection.setup.timeout.ms` in Kafka should address the Kafka consumer creation problem. However, the upsert process causing segment imbalance and subsequent query failures is a different issue.

Recommendations:
1. Update to the latest version that includes the Kafka fix.
2. Consider reducing the batch size and parallelism in your upserts to manage load more effectively.
3. Monitor the system for any new errors post-update and adjust configurations accordingly.
4. Open a new issue for the upsert causing segment imbalance for focused troubleshooting.

Hope this helps!
